football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Texas State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 7.0 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.

When Texas State has the ball (third down): Texas State’s offense converts 54.1% of its third downs, and Colorado State’s defense allows opponents to convert 56.4% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).
contradicting: When Colorado State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Colorado State’s offense has allowed a sack on 1.0% of its dropbacks, and Texas State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 4.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

In his last two games (UTSA and Oregon State), Farrar averaged 7.0 yards per attempt, against 4.2 in his two games before that.
